comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] This DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section is primarily proxy governance/executive compensation boilerplate with very limited SIFI-material content. Key observations:

1. NO off-balance-sheet SPVs, JVs, or project finance entities mentioned.
2. NO named customer concentration disclosures beyond general Fortune 100 references.
3. NO named supplier dependencies or single-source risks.
4. NO AI lab investments or equity stakes disclosed in this section.
5. NO related-party transactions of SIFI materiality beyond standard board interlocks (Sachin Mehra is CFO of Mastercard — noted as director but no material related-party transaction disclosed).
6. The peer group change (removing Amazon, Alphabet, Apple, Meta; adding AMD, Broadcom, Palo Alto Networks, Qualcomm) is notable as a governance signal but not a direct financial risk.
7. The Agentforce/Data Cloud $900M ARR growing 120% YoY on a $37.9B revenue base is strategically important context but not yet a SIFI concentration risk.
8. ValueAct Capital's Mason Morfit is now Chair of the Compensation Committee — an activist investor in a board governance role worth monitoring for future strategic pressure.

Overall: minimal SIFI-material extractions warranted from this section. The filing section is standard DEF 14A proxy governance content.
[chunk 2/3] This DEF 14A Comp Discussion section is largely governance/compensation boilerplate with limited SIFI-material content. Key signals extracted:

1. GOVERNANCE CONFLICT — Robin Washington simultaneously served as Salesforce Board member (Lead Independent Director, Audit Chair) AND sits on Alphabet's board (current), then was appointed Salesforce President & COFO in March 2025. This creates a potential related-party / independence tension, particularly given Alphabet is a major Salesforce competitor/partner in cloud and AI.

2. ACTIVIST COMP CHAIR — Mason Morfit (ValueAct Capital Co-CEO/CIO, $10B+ AUM) chairs the Compensation Committee after ValueAct took an activist position in Salesforce (Jan 2023 Form 8-K cited). Comp design being led by an active activist investor is a governance-layer risk signal worth monitoring for compensation structures that may prioritize margin extraction over R&D/growth investment.

3. AGENTFORCE EXECUTION — Compensation program was "realigned to support Agentforce objectives" — indicating performance metrics are now tied to a product that is described as early-stage and among "fastest-growing" but not yet at scale. No revenue concentration or counterparty data disclosed in this section.

No SPVs, off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, AI lab investments, or revenue roundtripping patterns were disclosed in this section.
[chunk 3/3] This DEF 14A section (Compensation Discussion & Analysis) for Salesforce (CRM) is almost entirely boilerplate executive compensation disclosure — say-on-pay vote outcomes, peer group changes, PRSU/RSU/option mix, perquisite caps, stock ownership guidelines, and compensation consultant engagements (Compensia, Semler Brossy). None of the content rises to SIFI-material threshold: there are no named customer/supplier concentrations, no SPVs or off-balance-sheet entities, no equity investments in AI labs or counterparties, no capex commitments with named counterparties, and no related-party transactions. The only potentially relevant business metrics mentioned are: revenue $37.9B FY2025, operating cash flow $13.1B, RPO $63.4B, and Data Cloud/AI ARR $900M (+120% YoY) — but these are performance highlights without counterparty-web implications. ValueAct Capital (via Mason Morfit as Comp Committee Chair) is a notable activist investor presence but does not constitute a SIFI-material related-party arrangement requiring extraction. No edges can be drawn that are not purely boilerplate. Extracting a minimal Salesforce company node for registry completeness only.

fields.purpose: Charitable philanthropy via 1-1-1 model (people, technology, resources)
fields.verbatim_quote: In January 1999, the Salesforce Foundation, also referred to as the Foundation, was chartered on an idea of leveraging the Company's people, technology and resources to help improve communities around the world. The Company calls this integrated philanthropic approach the 1-1-1 model. In connection with its 2019 business combination with Salesforce.org, the Company agreed to use its best efforts to make charitable cash contributions of up to $5 million to the Foundation in each fiscal quarter beginning in the third quarter of fiscal 2020 for ten years.

fields.category: Related-party transaction / private aircraft use perquisite
fields.verbatim_quote: In fiscal 2021, Mr. Benioff entered into a Time Sharing Agreement with the Company providing for the reimbursement by the Company to Mr. Benioff for business use of his personal aircraft. For fiscal 2025, the value of this reimbursement (excluding a portion reported in "All Other Compensation" in the Summary Compensation Table) was approximately $188,923.

For Mr. Benioff, this amount represents an allocation of costs paid by the Company for security arrangements provided for Mr. Benioff that are in addition to security arrangements provided while at work or on business travel. For fiscal 2025, this amount reflects certain ongoing security expenses allocable to the Company which, prior to fiscal 2024, were not invoiced to the Company.
